correctness.rationale: The rank-36 degree-seven multiplication test is an exact projective-geometric smoothness criterion. Exhaustive projective orbit enumeration accounts for 7,174,453 normalized quartics and gives 1,557 orbits. It finds 4,099,680 smooth equations in 805 orbits and seventeen exact rational ordinary-flex/hyperflex strata. An independent direct coefficient enumeration checks all normalized forms and rank-tests the 6,097 potentially seven-flex forms, leaving 936 smooth. A separately compiled cross-check reproduces all 1,557 orbit representatives, every exact contact count, and all seventeen weighted strata. The polynomial representative is checked explicitly for smoothness and seven flex contacts. All computational paths and input data are in the attached package; no unproved interpolation from a sample is used.

originality.rationale: The finite characteristic-three conic-support theorem and the previously compiled hyperflex-only census are acknowledged as covered. The claim is the previously unlocated complete joint ordinary-flex/hyperflex distribution on every smooth ternary F3 plane quartic, together with its single sharp seven-flex orbit. The compared primary sources concern conic support, point counting, or bitangents, and lack this joint contact invariant. Search and comparison do not prove absolute priority; the identified residual risks remain.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished finite-geometry flex-point table may give equivalent counts.
The full manuscripts of every historical flex paper and every private or external quartic database were not accessible; some stronger earlier classification might imply the table.
Computer-assisted finite exhaustive proof is fully reproducible but has not received external independent audit.

value.rationale: The ordinary rational flex count is a natural arithmetic geometric contact invariant of canonical genus-three plane quartics. Its joint spectrum with hyperflexes is not determined by the known characteristic-three flex conic, the point census or the previously recorded hyperflex marginal. The exhaustive classification isolates one sharp seven-flex projective orbit and supplies an explicit smooth representative whose seven rational points are flexes. These are motivated incidence data and a natural exceptional geometry, not an arbitrary slice, trivial substitution or a tiny unmotivated adjustment. Relevance is restricted to F3 and no general theorem is asserted.
